qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Quotations (RFQ) issued by NYS Office of General Services for an Aggregate Hardware Buy, including submission deadlines, scope of work, evaluation criteria, and procurement terms.

quotes.quote: RFQ Title Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 RFQ Number 20-01
Request for Quotations 20-01 Aggregate Hardware Buy

OGS is seeking competitive quotes from Contract holders of the OGS Group 73600 Award 22802 Information Technology Umbrella Contract – Manufacturer Based (Statewide) (“Manufacturer Umbrella Contract”) for the Lots indicated below.

OGS is releasing this Request for Quotes (RFQ) for Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 (“RFQ 20-01”). The purpose of RFQ 20-01 is to establish an award for each Configuration as set forth in Attachment A - Technical Response.

Quotes and pricing submitted in response to RFQ 20-01 must remain open and valid for at least one hundred-twenty (120) calendar days from the date that RFQ Submissions are due, unless the time for making an award is extended by mutual consent of OGS and the Contractor.

findings.title: Customer Service Response Time

quotes.quote: These records will be made available on request, no more than fifteen (15) business days after request, in a searchable electronic format as specified by OGS.

findings.title: Additional Products Not Factored into Evaluation
findings.fact: Pricing for Additional Products will not be factored into the evaluation.

quotes.quote: Pricing for any Additional Products will not be factored into the evaluation, but submission of items for review at the time of bid will facilitate the availability of Additional Products for Authorized Users as part of a Configuration at time of award.

findings.title: Evaluation of Standard Configuration Pricing
findings.fact: Standard Configuration pricing is evaluated as part of the proposal.

quotes.quote: Contractors are encouraged to aggressively discount their pricing for the Standard Configurations.  Contractors shall provide itemized pricing on all Products offered in the Standard Configurations.

findings.title: Evaluation of Discount Percentages
findings.fact: Discount percentages are evaluated and must be expressed as a single value, not a range.

quotes.quote: All Discount percentage values shall not exceed two decimal places (for example: 20.25222% shall be rounded to nearest one hundredth 20.25%). findings.title: Awarded Standard Configuration Price Fixed for Term
findings.fact: The awarded Standard Configuration price and component prices will remain equal to the Agreement awarded price for the term and any extensions, though lower pricing may be offered at any time.

quotes.quote: The awarded Standard Configuration price and its component prices will remain equal to the Agreement awarded price for the term of the Agreement(s) and any extensions, though Contractor may offer lower pricing at any time on an individual transaction.

findings.title: Required Product Price Stability
findings.fact: Required Product prices awarded shall remain equal to or better than the originally awarded price throughout the life of the Agreement, though lower pricing may be offered at any time.

findings.title: Extension of Agreement to Other Jurisdictions
findings.fact: The Agreement pricing may be extended to other states or governmental jurisdictions upon mutual written agreement, with New York State reserving the right to negotiate additional discounts.

quotes.quote: This Agreement Pricing may be extended to additional States or Governmental jurisdictions upon mutual written agreement between New York State (the lead contracting State) and the Contractor.
New York State reserves the right to negotiate additional discounts based on any increased volume generated by such extensions.

findings.title: EPEAT Certification Requirements
findings.fact: Desktops, laptops, and monitors must meet EPEAT Silver certification, while interactive displays must meet EPEAT Bronze, with quarterly reporting required.

findings.title: Only Lot 2 Hardware Contractors Eligible
findings.fact: RFQ 20-01 is only distributed to Contractors holding an award for Lot 2 – Hardware on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract. Quotes will only be accepted from Lot 2 Contractors; Resellers are not eligible and will be disqualified.
findings.business_implication: Only contractors with an existing Lot 2 Hardware award on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract can participate. Resellers are excluded, so if your company is a reseller, you cannot bid. This limits the competition to direct manufacturers or their authorized contractors.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that your company holds a valid Lot 2 Hardware award on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract before investing time in preparing a bid. If you are a reseller, do not submit a bid as it will be disqualified.

quotes.quote: Quotes from Resellers will not be accepted. Contractors must have an award for Lot 2 to bid on this RFQ.

RFQ 20-01 is only being distributed to Contractors holding an award for Lot 2 – Hardware on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract (“Contractors”). Quotes under RFQ 20-01 will only be accepted from Lot 2 Contractors on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract; Resellers are not eligible to respond and any bids from a Reseller will be disqualified.

findings.title: Products Must Be on Lot 2 Price List
findings.fact: All proposed products must be on the Contractor's Lot 2 - Hardware price list at the time of the RFQ Submission due date.
findings.business_implication: The products you offer must already be listed on your Lot 2 Hardware price list. If you propose products not on the list, your bid may be rejected. This ensures that all offered products are pre-approved under the umbrella contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Review your current Lot 2 Hardware price list to ensure all products you intend to propose are included. If any product is missing, consider adding it to your price list before the submission deadline, if possible.

quotes.quote: All Products proposed as part of the Standard Configuration and Products proposed for Required Products, as well as any Additional Products, must be on the Contractor's Lot 2 - Hardware price list at the time of the RFQ Submission due date.

findings.title: Bid Validity Period
findings.fact: Quotes and pricing must remain valid for at least 120 calendar days from the due date, unless extended by mutual consent.
findings.business_implication: Your pricing must remain firm for at least 120 days after the submission deadline. This means you cannot change your prices during this period, which could be a risk if costs change. However, it also shows commitment to the bid.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure your pricing is sustainable for at least 120 days. Consider potential cost fluctuations and set your prices accordingly. Be prepared to hold your bid open for the full validity period.

quotes.quote: Quotes and pricing submitted in response to RFQ 20-01 must remain open and valid for at least one hundred-twenty (120) calendar days from the date that RFQ Submissions are due, unless the time for making an award is extended by mutual consent of OGS and the Contractor.

findings.title: Submission Requirements
findings.fact: Submissions must include Attachment A – Technical Response, Attachment D – Issue Escalation Plan, and Manufacturer Information Page, on two USB flash drives.
findings.business_implication: The submission must be on two USB flash drives and include specific documents. Failure to provide all required documents or using the wrong format could lead to rejection. This is a mandatory requirement.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare two USB flash drives with the required documents: Attachment A, Attachment D, and the Manufacturer Information Page. Ensure they are clearly labeled and not password protected. Double-check that all documents are complete and in the required format.

quotes.quote: Two (2) digital storage devices (USB flash drive), clearly labeled, shall contain the following documents, completed in their entirety: • Attachment A – Technical Response • Attachment D – Issue Escalation Plan • Manufacturer Information Page (Last page of this Document)

findings.fact: The RFQ is open only to Contractors holding a Manufacturer Umbrella Contract with OGS.
findings.business_implication: Only contractors with a Manufacturer Umbrella Contract can bid. This is a prerequisite for participation. If you do not hold such a contract, you cannot submit a bid.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm that your company holds a Manufacturer Umbrella Contract with OGS. If not, you are not eligible to participate. If you do, ensure you have the necessary Lot 2 award as well.

findings.business_implication: Products must meet specific environmental standards to be eligible for the contract. Failure to comply could result in disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that all proposed products have the required EPEAT certification and maintain documentation for submission.

findings.business_implication: Bids involving restricted entities will be rejected, potentially impacting supply chain and product availability.
findings.action_recommendation: Screen all components and suppliers against the restricted lists to ensure compliance and avoid disqualification.

quotes.quote: OGS will not accept a bid from a Contractor, or a Contractor product that contains products made by an entity on any of the lists maintained by the US Customs and Border Patrol at the link set out below.

findings.business_implication: Award is contingent on agreeing to participate in the eMarketplace, which may require additional setup and resources.

findings.title: Delivery Period and Extensions
findings.fact: The awarded contractor must deliver units within 45 calendar days of receipt of a Purchase Order, with possible extensions up to 60 calendar days and beyond with OGS approval.
findings.business_implication: This delivery timeline is a contractual obligation. Failure to meet it could result in penalties or loss of business. Understanding the extension process is crucial for managing potential delays.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess your supply chain capabilities to ensure you can meet the 45-day delivery requirement. If there is risk of delay, plan to request an extension promptly. Familiarize yourself with the extension request process and the criteria for OGS approval.

quotes.quote: The Awarded Contractor(s) shall deliver the units ordered by an Authorized User within forty-five (45) calendar days of receipt of a Purchase Order unless either the Authorized User or OGS grants an extension of time as provided below.

If upon receipt of a Purchase Order the Awarded Contractor determines it cannot meet the 45 calendar day delivery period the Awarded Contractor may submit a written request to the Authorized User to extend the required Product delivery period to up to sixty (60) calendar days.

findings.title: Stage 1 Administrative Review
findings.fact: Stage 1 reviews Attachment A, Attachment D, and Manufacturer Information page for completeness. Alterations to documents are prohibited and may result in rejection.
findings.business_implication: Any unauthorized modifications to the provided templates could lead to immediate disqualification. This is a pass/fail stage, so compliance is mandatory.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that all documents are filled out exactly as provided, without altering any formulas, worksheets, or formatting. Double-check that all required fields are completed. Train staff on the strict no-alteration policy.

quotes.quote: The submitted Attachment A – Technical Response, Attachment D – Issue Escalation Plan, and the Manufacturer Information page (last page of this document) will be reviewed for completeness. The addition or deletion of worksheets, columns, unlocking the document, rewriting formulas, or similar alterations to any document is prohibited. OGS reserves the right to reject any Contractor Submission or portion(s) thereof determined to have been altered/modified by the Contractor from the original format. Failure to provide fully completed documents may result in rejection of the RFQ Response without further review.

findings.title: Stage 2 Technical Evaluation
findings.fact: Stage 2 compares Attachment A to Standard Configuration and Required Products requirements. All proposed SKUs must be on the Contractor's approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List. Configurations with SKUs not on the price list may not proceed.
findings.business_implication: Bidders must ensure every SKU they propose is already on their approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List before submission. Any SKU not on the list will cause the entire configuration to be disqualified from further evaluation, potentially losing the opportunity for that configuration.
findings.action_recommendation: Before submitting, cross-check all proposed SKUs against the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List. If any SKU is missing, either add it via a Contract Modification request (prioritized by OGS if indicated for this RFQ) or replace it with an approved SKU. Ensure all SKUs are on the list prior to the RFQ submission due date.

quotes.quote: Submitted Attachment A – Technical Response will be compared to Standard Configuration and Required Products requirements. All proposed SKUs for proposed products offered in Attachment A – Technical Response must be on the Contractor’s approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List. Any Configuration that contains a SKU that is not included on the Manufacturer’s Umbrella Contract Price List may not proceed further in the evaluation process.

findings.title: Stage 3 Financial Evaluation
findings.fact: Only Contractors whose Standard Configuration specifications and Required Products pass review proceed to financial evaluation. Attachment C is created from Attachment A and used for financial evaluation.
findings.business_implication: Bidders must pass the technical evaluation to be considered for financial evaluation. The financial response (Attachment C) is pre-populated from the technical response (Attachment A), so any errors or omissions in Attachment A will directly impact the financial evaluation and could lead to rejection.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure Attachment A is complete and accurate, as it will be used to generate Attachment C. Review all technical specifications and required products carefully to avoid any missing or incorrect information that could cause failure in the technical evaluation and prevent progression to the financial stage.

quotes.quote: Only Contractors whose Standard Configuration specifications and Required Products pass review, as determined by OGS, will proceed to the evaluation of Attachment C – Financial Response for those specific Configurations. For those Contractors who have been determined to have passed the Technical Evaluation, their Attachment A - Technical Response will be used to create the Attachment C – Financial Response and be provided to the Contractor in order to complete and submit. The proposed pricing on Attachment C – Financial Response will then be used in the Financial Evaluation.

findings.title: Mandatory Products and Evaluation Components
findings.fact: All components within Standard Configuration and Required Products are mandatory. Failure to complete required fields may result in rejection. Only items with mandatory specifications are evaluated for technical evaluation; additional items are reviewed only for inclusion in Lot 2.
findings.business_implication: Bidders must complete every required field in Attachment A and Attachment C; any missing information can lead to outright rejection. Additionally, only items with mandatory specifications are technically evaluated, but all additional items must still be on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List (Lot 2) to be included; otherwise, they will be removed from the response.
findings.action_recommendation: Thoroughly review Attachment A and Attachment C to ensure all mandatory fields are filled. For additional items listed in Section A of Attachment A, verify they are included in Lot 2 of the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract; if not, either add them via contract modification or remove them from the response to avoid issues.

quotes.quote: ALL COMPONENTS WITHIN THE STANDARD CONFIGURATION AND ITS REQUIRED PRODUCTS ARE MANDATORY. Failure to complete all required fields in Attachment A – Technical Response or Attachment C – Financial Response may result in rejection of the RFQ Response without further review.

Only items that have a mandatory specification will be evaluated for the Technical Evaluation, additional items needed to create the Standard Configuration listed in Section A of Attachment A will be reviewed only to determine if the items are included in Lot 2 of the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract.

findings.title: Basis for Award
findings.fact: Awards are made to the responsive and responsible Contractor(s) with the highest Total Financial Score per Configuration that meets all specified technical requirements. The same awardee can be awarded multiple Configurations.
findings.business_implication: Bidders must be both technically compliant and financially competitive to win. Since awards are per configuration, a bidder can win multiple configurations if they offer the highest total financial score for each. This means bidders should strategically price each configuration to maximize their chances across multiple awards.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a pricing strategy for each configuration that balances competitiveness with profitability. Ensure all technical requirements are met for each configuration bid. Consider bidding on multiple configurations to increase the chance of winning at least one, and potentially multiple, awards.

quotes.quote: OGS will separately evaluate and separately make awards for each Configuration. Awards will be made to the responsive and responsible Contractor(s) with the highest Total Financial Score per Configuration that meets all the specified technical requirements. The same awardee can be awarded multiple Configurations.

findings.title: Evaluation of Required Products Pricing
findings.fact: Required Products pricing will be factored into the final Quote price for evaluation.
findings.business_implication: The pricing for Required Products directly impacts the total financial score, as it is included in the final quote price used for evaluation. Aggressive discounting on Required Products can improve the bidder's competitiveness, but must still be profitable and compliant with the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract pricing (cannot exceed Net NYS Contract Price).
findings.action_recommendation: Consider offering aggressive discounts on Required Products to lower the total quote price and increase the total financial score. Ensure that the discounted pricing is still above cost and complies with the requirement that pricing must be equal to or better than the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price. Balance discounts to maximize score while maintaining profitability.

quotes.quote: Contractors are encouraged to aggressively discount their pricing for their Required Products, as the pricing will be factored in the final Quote price for evaluation.

findings.title: Evaluation of Required Products Discounts
findings.fact: The discount percentages bid on Required Products will be factored into the evaluation.
findings.business_implication: The discount percentages offered on Required Products directly influence the evaluation score and final pricing competitiveness. Aggressive discounts can improve the bid's standing but may reduce profit margins.
findings.action_recommendation: Strategically set discount percentages for Required Products to balance competitiveness with profitability, considering the long-term impact on pricing for Additional Products in the same category.

quotes.quote: Contractors are required to provide discount percentages that will apply to each of the three (3) Required Products.  The discount that is bid on the single Product shall apply to all Additional Products in the same Required Product category, as described in Section 7.3.5 – Additional Product Discount. Contractors are encouraged to aggressively discount their pricing for their Required Products, as the pricing will be factored in the final Quote price for evaluation.

findings.title: Pricing Requirements for Standard Configurations
findings.fact: Contractors must provide itemized pricing for all products in Standard Configurations, and quoted pricing cannot exceed the Net NYS Contract Price on the Manufacturer's Umbrella Contract.
findings.business_implication: Pricing for Standard Configurations must be at or below the umbrella contract prices, ensuring cost competitiveness but potentially limiting profit margins. Non-compliance could lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all itemized pricing for Standard Configurations is set at or below the Net NYS Contract Price, and verify that all SKUs are on the umbrella contract price list before submission.

quotes.quote: Contractors shall provide itemized pricing on all Products offered in the Standard Configurations.  In no event may quoted pricing exceed the Net NYS Contract Price on the Manufacturer’s Umbrella Contract.

Contractors shall provide itemized pricing on all Products offered in the Standard Configurations.  In no event may quoted pricing exceed the Net NYS Contract Price on the Manufacturer’s Umbrella Contract.

findings.title: Discount Percentage Requirements for Required Products
findings.fact: Contractors must bid discount percentages for each of the three Required Product categories, and these percentages may be increased but not decreased during the term of the Agreement.
findings.business_implication: The discount percentages bid at the outset are binding for the contract term; they can only be increased, not decreased, which could affect future profitability if costs rise.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully calculate discount percentages for Required Products to ensure they are sustainable over the contract term, considering potential cost fluctuations and the inability to lower them later.

quotes.quote: Contractors are required to provide discount percentages that will apply to each of the three (3) Required Products.  The discount that is bid on the single Product shall apply to all Additional Products in the same Required Product category, as described in Section 7.3.5 – Additional Product Discount. Contractors are encouraged to aggressively discount their pricing for their Required Products, as the pricing will be factored in the final Quote price for evaluation.  The discount percentages may be increased, but not decreased during the term of the Agreement and any extensions.

findings.title: Discount Percentage Application to Additional Products
findings.fact: The same discount percentages bid for Required Product categories apply to Additional Products in their respective categories, and these percentages may be increased but not decreased.
findings.business_implication: Discounts on Required Products will automatically extend to Additional Products in the same category, affecting overall pricing and margins. This can be advantageous for winning bids but may reduce profitability on a wider range of products.
findings.action_recommendation: When setting discount percentages for Required Products, consider the impact on Additional Products in the same category, and ensure the discounts are viable for the entire product line.

quotes.quote: Contractors shall provide the same awarded discount percentages that applied to the three (3) Required Product categories (Warranty and Services, Components, and Peripherals), to the Additional Products in their respective categories.  For all Additional Products, the discount percentages will apply to the Net NYS Contract Price from the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List. At time of award, these discount percentages will apply to the original Additional Products bid and any future Additional Products added within the scope of the Agreement. Only Additional Products approved by OGS for inclusion on the awarded Configuration Price List may be offered under any resulting Agreement. Discount percentages may be increased, but not decreased during the term of the Agreement and any extensions.

findings.title: Pricing Must Be Equal to or Better Than Umbrella Contract
findings.fact: All pricing offered on Attachment C must be equal to or better than the pricing for the same SKU on the Contractor's Manufacturer Umbrella Contract.
findings.business_implication: Pricing on Attachment C must be at or below the umbrella contract prices, ensuring competitiveness but potentially limiting profit margins. Failure to comply may result in rejection.
findings.action_recommendation: Review all pricing on Attachment C to ensure it is equal to or better than the corresponding umbrella contract prices, and make necessary adjustments before submission.

quotes.quote: All pricing offered on Attachment C - Financial Response must be equal to or better than the pricing offered for that SKU on the Contractor's Manufacturer Umbrella Contract.

findings.title: Estimated Spend and IDIQ Nature
findings.fact: The estimated dollar value of the aggregated award is approximately $40 million, but the agreements are Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with no guarantee of volume or dollar value.
findings.business_implication: The $40 million estimate is not a commitment; actual orders may be significantly lower or higher. Bidders should not rely on this figure for capacity planning or revenue projections.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the risk of low order volumes and ensure pricing is competitive to maximize order potential. Avoid over-investing in inventory or resources based solely on the estimate.

quotes.quote: The estimated dollar value of the aggregated award of the fourteen (14) Standard Configurations in this RFQ, based on historical purchases under previous awards, is approximately $40 million.
However, the Agreements resulting from this RFQ will be Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) awards.
There is no guarantee of volume to be purchased
There is no guarantee of dollar value to be purchased

findings.title: eMarketplace Participation Requirement
findings.fact: Contractors awarded a Configuration must provide a hosted or punch-out catalog via the NYS eMarketplace, with no fees for mandatory participation, but optional ERP integration may incur fees.
findings.business_implication: Mandatory participation in the eMarketplace is required for award, but there are no fees for the basic catalog. However, if the bidder wants to integrate their ERP system, additional costs will be incurred.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for the eMarketplace catalog setup and ensure compliance. Evaluate the costs and benefits of optional ERP integration and decide whether to pursue it based on expected order volume.

quotes.quote: Contractors that are awarded a Configuration under the Aggregate Agreement should provide a “hosted” or “punch-out” catalog that is available to Authorized Users via the NYS eMarketplace.
There are no fees required for a Contractor’s mandatory participation in the catalog site development or management.
However, Contractors who wish to integrate their ERP system with the NYS eMarketplace can do so for an additional fee.

findings.title: Term and Extension Options
findings.fact: The Agreement term is one year, with OGS having the right to extend for up to an additional year, and a possible short-term extension of up to three months (or six with contractor concurrence).
findings.business_implication: The contract term is relatively short (one year) but could be extended up to two years or more. This provides potential for longer-term revenue but also uncertainty regarding the actual duration.
findings.action_recommendation: Consider the potential for extensions when planning resources and pricing. Be prepared for possible extensions and ensure that pricing remains competitive throughout the potential extended term.

quotes.quote: The term of the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement shall be one (1) year.

OGS reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to extend all or some Configurations of the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement for a period up to an additional one (1) year upon written notice to the Contractor.
OGS reserves the right to seek an additional short-term extension for the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement in accordance with Manufacturer Umbrella Contract, Section 5, Short Term Extension:

findings.title: Reseller Usage and Responsibilities
findings.fact: Contractors may use Resellers for fulfillment, but must receive payment and invoice directly; Contractors remain wholly responsible for Reseller actions.
findings.business_implication: Using resellers can help with fulfillment, but the contractor retains full responsibility for all actions and performance. This introduces potential risks if resellers fail to meet obligations.
findings.action_recommendation: If using resellers, ensure they are reliable and contractually bound to meet the same standards. Maintain oversight and have contingency plans to mitigate risks.

quotes.quote: Contractors are permitted to use Resellers in the fulfillment of orders under any resulting Aggregate Agreement.
Contractors must receive payment from Authorized Users directly and must invoice Authorized Users directly.

Contractors remain wholly and solely responsible for the actions of the Resellers acting on their behalf as part of the aggregate purchase, as well as the performance of all Products, and conformity with the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract and any agreement resulting from this RFQ.

findings.title: Price List Modification Procedures
findings.fact: Contractors can modify pricing and products through specific procedures, including lowering prices, adding/deleting products, and replacing products, with conditions such as EOL notice and price constraints.
findings.business_implication: The ability to modify pricing and products provides flexibility, but there are strict procedures and constraints, such as EOL notice requirements and price caps for replacements. This could impact the ability to adjust offerings quickly.
findings.action_recommendation: Familiarize with the modification procedures and ensure compliance. Plan for EOL events and submit necessary notices in a timely manner to avoid disruptions.

quotes.quote: The Awarded Contractor is authorized to provide the Standard Configuration(s), Required Products, and Additional Products initially awarded in the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement. Products included under the Agreement can be modified through the processes described in RFQ 20-01, Appendix 2 – Agreement Price List Modification Procedures and utilizing RFQ 20-01, Appendix 3 - Pricing Modification Form.
All Product pricing on the Contractor’s Aggregate Buy 20-01 Price List can be lowered at any time throughout the term of the Agreement and any extensions.
Additional Products can only be removed from the Agreement if the Products are shown to OGS’s satisfaction to be incompatible with the Standard Configurations, or at End of Life (EOL).
The replacement Product must be offered on the Aggregate Agreement Price List at the same or lower Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement pricing as the Product it is replacing.

findings.title: Sales Reporting and Administrative Fee
findings.fact: Contractors must submit quarterly sales reports and pay an administrative fee of 0.50% on all sales, with penalties for underpayment.
findings.business_implication: This imposes ongoing administrative and financial obligations. The 0.50% fee reduces profit margins on all sales, and the penalty clause for underpayment (audit costs or three times the discrepancy) creates significant financial risk if reporting is inaccurate.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust sales tracking and reporting processes to ensure accuracy and timeliness. Set aside funds for the administrative fee and consider internal audits to avoid penalties.

quotes.quote: The awarded Contractor(s) shall provide OGS with accurate and timely sales reports containing detailed information of all purchases by State and non-state Authorized Users, political subdivisions and other authorized entities within other State or governmental jurisdictions, made pursuant to Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01.
The awarded Contractor(s) are required to pay an Administrative Fee in the amount of point five percent (0.50%) for all sales generated from this Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement.

If, as a result of any such audit, Administrative Fees are determined to have been underpaid by more than five percent (5%) for the period audited, Contractor shall pay the costs of such audit or three times the discrepancy, whichever is higher.

findings.title: OGS Not Liable for Bid Preparation Costs
findings.fact: OGS will not be held liable for any cost incurred by the Contractor for work performed in the preparation of a response to this RFQ.
findings.business_implication: The bidder bears all costs associated with preparing the response, with no reimbursement if the bid is unsuccessful. This is a sunk cost risk.
findings.action_recommendation: Budget for bid preparation costs and ensure that the potential contract value justifies the investment. Avoid over-spending on proposal development.

quotes.quote: OGS will not be held liable for any cost incurred by the Contractor for work performed in the preparation of a response to this Request for Quote (RFQ).

findings.title: Contractor Responsible for Replacement of Incompatible Components
findings.fact: Replacement components within the Aggregate Hardware Buy RFQ 20-01 must be compatible with RFQ 20-01 peripherals or the Contractor will be responsible for replacement of both the component and the peripheral.
findings.business_implication: If a replacement component is not compatible with existing peripherals, the contractor must replace both at its own cost, leading to potential financial losses and operational disruptions.
findings.action_recommendation: Thoroughly test replacement components for compatibility with all peripherals before offering them. Maintain a list of compatible peripherals and ensure replacements meet specifications.

quotes.quote: Replacement components within the Aggregate Hardware Buy RFQ 20-01 must be compatible with RFQ 20-01 peripherals or the Contractor will be responsible for replacement of both the component and the peripheral.

findings.title: Contractor Liable for Reporting Inaccuracies
findings.fact: If inaccuracies of more than 5% are found in any of the reporting documents, Contractors shall pay the cost of such audit or three times the discrepancy, whichever is higher.
findings.business_implication: Inaccurate reporting can lead to severe financial penalties, including audit costs or treble damages, which could be substantial and damage profitability.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement rigorous internal controls and verification processes for all reporting documents. Consider periodic internal audits to ensure accuracy and avoid penalties.

quotes.quote: As a result of such review, if inaccuracies of more than 5% are found in any of the reporting documents, Contractors shall pay the cost of such audit or three times the discrepancy, whichever is higher.

findings.title: Contractor Responsible for Warranty Replacements
findings.fact: If a unit becomes inoperable within the warranty window and cannot be repaired, a brand new unit shall be provided at no charge. Contractors shall not provide refurbished or remanufactured equipment as they are not allowed under this Aggregate Hardware Buy.
findings.business_implication: This imposes a strict warranty obligation: providing brand new replacements at no cost, which could be expensive if failures occur. It also prohibits using refurbished units, limiting cost-saving options.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure warranty terms are factored into pricing. Maintain adequate inventory of new units for replacements and establish efficient processes for data transfer and replacement.

quotes.quote: If a unit becomes inoperable within the warranty window and cannot be repaired, a brand new unit shall be provided at no charge. Contractors shall not provide refurbished or remanufactured equipment as they are not allowed under this Aggregate Hardware Buy.

findings.title: Contractor Responsible for Network Integrity
findings.fact: Connections to the Authorized User’s networks must be performed in a manner prescribed by an Authorized User to preserve the integrity of the Authorized User’s network, confidentiality and integrity of information transmitted over that Authorized User’s network, and the availability of the network.
findings.business_implication: The contractor bears significant responsibility for network security and availability when connecting to Authorized User networks. Any failure could lead to liability for breaches, downtime, or data loss, potentially resulting in financial penalties, legal action, or termination.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that all network connection procedures are strictly followed as per Authorized User specifications. Implement robust security measures, train staff on compliance, and obtain clear instructions for each connection. Consider cybersecurity insurance to mitigate potential liabilities.

quotes.quote: Connections to the Authorized User’s networks must be performed in a manner prescribed by an Authorized User to preserve the integrity of the Authorized User’s network, confidentiality and integrity of information transmitted over that Authorized User’s network, and the availability of the network.

findings.title: Term and Extension of Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement
findings.fact: The term of the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement shall be one (1) year, with OGS reserving the right to extend all or some Configurations for up to an additional one (1) year upon written notice. Additionally, OGS may seek a short-term extension in accordance with Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Section 5, allowing unilateral extension for up to three (3) months, or up to six (6) months with Contractor concurrence, terminating if a replacement Agreement is issued.
findings.business_implication: The contract term is relatively short (1 year) with potential extensions at OGS's discretion. This creates uncertainty in revenue forecasting and resource planning. The contractor must be prepared for possible extensions or abrupt termination if a replacement agreement is issued.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop flexible operational plans to accommodate potential extensions. Maintain good performance to encourage OGS to exercise extension options. Monitor contract timelines and communicate with OGS regarding extension intentions. Prepare for possible transition if a replacement agreement is issued.

quotes.quote: The term of the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement shall be one (1) year.  The term shall not commence until OGS execution and posting of the final executed documents to the Awarded Contractor(s).  OGS reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to extend all or some Configurations of the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement for a period up to an additional one (1) year upon written notice to the Contractor.

OGS reserves the right to seek an additional short-term extension for the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement in accordance with Manufacturer Umbrella Contract, Section 5, Short Term Extension: In the event a replacement Agreement has not been issued, any Agreement let and awarded hereunder by the State, may be extended unilaterally by the State for an additional period of up to three (3) months upon notice to the Awarded Contractor with the same terms and conditions as the original Agreement including, but not limited to, prices and delivery requirements.  With the concurrence of the Awarded Contractor, the extension may be for a period of up to six (6) months in lieu of three (3) months.  However, this extension terminates should the replacement Agreement be issued in the interim.

findings.title: Termination for Delivery Delays
findings.fact: OGS reserves the right to terminate the Agreement in whole or in part if it becomes aware of multiple incidents of delays in delivery.
findings.business_implication: Multiple delivery delays can lead to termination of the entire agreement or parts of it, resulting in loss of revenue and potential damage to the contractor's reputation. This clause emphasizes the importance of reliable supply chain management.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust delivery tracking and management systems to ensure on-time delivery. Proactively communicate any potential delays to OGS and Authorized Users. Maintain buffer stock and alternative suppliers to mitigate risks. Regularly review delivery performance metrics.

quotes.quote: If OGS becomes aware of multiple incidents of delays in delivery, OGS reserves the right to terminate the Agreement in whole or in part.

findings.title: Termination for Failure to Submit Accurate Sales Reports
findings.fact: Failure to submit accurate sales reports on a timely basis may result in termination of the Contractor's Manufacturer Umbrella Contract in whole or in part and activation of Replacement Contractor.
findings.business_implication: Inaccurate or late sales reports can lead to termination of the umbrella contract, which would also affect the Aggregate Hardware Buy agreement. This could result in loss of the contract and potential financial penalties.
findings.action_recommendation: Establish a robust reporting process to ensure sales reports are accurate and submitted on time. Assign dedicated staff to handle reporting. Implement internal checks and audits to verify data accuracy. Stay updated on reporting requirements and deadlines.

quotes.quote: Failure to submit accurate reports on a timely basis may result in termination of the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract in whole or in part and activation 7.23 Replacement Contractor.

findings.title: Termination for Audit Underpayments
findings.fact: Failure to make payments or repeated errors on subsequent audits may lead to termination of this Agreement in whole or in part, after which OGS reserves the right to award to the second-place contractor.
findings.business_implication: Underpayment of administrative fees or repeated audit errors can lead to termination and replacement by a competitor. This poses a significant financial and reputational risk.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure accurate calculation and timely payment of administrative fees. Maintain thorough records to support sales reports and fee calculations. Conduct internal audits to identify and correct discrepancies before OGS audits. Respond promptly to any audit findings.

quotes.quote: Failure to make such payments or repeated errors on subsequent audits may result in the scheduling of a responsibility meeting in relation to Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract, and may lead to termination of this Agreement in whole or in part, after which OGS reserves the right to award to the second-place contractor.

findings.title: Delivery Delay Reporting Ambiguity
findings.fact: The document states that the Contractor must submit a monthly report of any delays in delivery using Appendix 5, but also states that the Contractor must submit along with Appendix 1 – Sales Report Form a report of any and all deliveries that fall outside the 45-day period. This creates ambiguity regarding the required reporting mechanism for delivery delays.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity in reporting requirements for delivery delays could lead to inadvertent non-compliance, potentially resulting in penalties or termination of the agreement. It also creates administrative burden and confusion for the contractor's reporting processes.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from OGS to determine the exact reporting mechanism for delivery delays. If both reports are required, establish a process to ensure both are submitted accurately and on time. Document all communications with OGS regarding this ambiguity.

quotes.quote: Contractor shall submit a monthly report to OGS of any delays in delivery by using Appendix 5.
Contractor must submit, along with Appendix 1 – Sales Report Form, a report of any and all deliveries that fall outside the 45-day period stated in Section 7.14 Product Delivery.
